{"rewrites":[{"sql":"SELECT o.user_id, count(1) AS order_count, sum(o.total_cents) AS spent FROM public.orders o WHERE o.status = $1 GROUP BY o.user_id HAVING count(1) > $2 ORDER BY spent DESC","transformation":"Replace count(*) with count(1); both count non-null rows identically since the row itself is never null, so aggregates and the HAVING filter are unchanged.","assumptions":[]},{"sql":"SELECT t.user_id, t.order_count, t.spent FROM (SELECT o.user_id, count(*) AS order_count, sum(o.total_cents) AS spent FROM public.orders o WHERE o.status = $1 GROUP BY o.user_id) t WHERE t.order_count > $2 ORDER BY t.spent DESC","transformation":"Move the HAVING predicate into an outer WHERE on the pre-computed aggregate, letting the aggregate finish before filtering; the result set is identical because the outer filter compares the same count value.","assumptions":[{"kind":"not_null","table":"public.orders","column":"user_id"}]},{"sql":"SELECT o.user_id, count(*) FILTER (WHERE o.status = $1) AS order_count, sum(o.total_cents) FILTER (WHERE o.status = $1) AS spent FROM public.orders o GROUP BY o.user_id HAVING count(*) FILTER (WHERE o.status = $1) > $2 ORDER BY spent DESC","transformation":"Push the status equality into aggregate FILTER clauses over a full GROUP BY; each group's filtered aggregates see exactly the rows the original WHERE selected, so counts, sums, and the HAVING comparison are identical (groups whose filtered count is 0 or below the threshold are removed, matching the original which never emitted them; sum over an empty set would be NULL but such rows cannot survive the HAVING filter).","assumptions":[{"kind":"not_null","table":"public.orders","column":"user_id"},{"kind":"not_null","table":"public.orders","column":"status"}]}]}
